# Data Strategy - MPLAD Trace

## Two clearly separated tiers

**Tier 1: real public aggregate data.** `mp_fund_summary` holds public state, district, MP, and year-level MPLAD fund summaries. Derived utilization, unspent, and completion ratios are calculated from those real values.

**Tier 2: calibrated synthetic project data.** `projects` holds the work-level records generated by `data/generate_dataset.py`. Cost, timeline, contractor, and location fields are synthetic and must never be described as real government transaction records. The `_ground_truth_*` fields are evaluation labels only.

## Production database design

Postgres + PostGIS is authoritative; see `backend/schema.sql`. Project locations are stored as `GEOGRAPHY(POINT, 4326)` and have a GiST index. Geographic density is the count of other projects within 2km, computed with:

```sql
SELECT p1.project_id, COUNT(p2.project_id) AS nearby_count
FROM projects AS p1
LEFT JOIN projects AS p2
  ON p1.project_id <> p2.project_id
 AND ST_DWithin(p1.location, p2.location, 2000)
GROUP BY p1.project_id;
```

This avoids coordinate rounding and preserves indexed, meter-based spatial semantics. The Module 2 local CSV fallback uses the same exact-radius definition only to permit offline tests before ingestion; it is not the production implementation.

## Presentation framing

The macro layer uses real published aggregate data where available. The transaction-level demonstration is synthetic because granular work records require implementer-level eSAKSHI access. A deployed implementation would ingest authorized work records into the same PostGIS design.
